messages:
alex_sales: Quick sync — FinCorp POC ask: they want Redwood Private deployed in their account via VPC endpoint (interface) + our control plane private link. No internet egress from model hosts; all outbound must go through their NAT/egress firewall. Can ops/eng confirm feasibility and steps?

mike_solutions: They also asked about routes for cross-account VPC peering vs VPCE. Preference is VPCE (interface) to keep control-plane comms private, but they want certs and DNS validated.

eli_engineering: Possible. High-level: 1) Customer creates VPC (or reuse). 2) Create interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.<region>.vpce) for Redwood control plane if needed OR we request a VPC endpoint service (ours) and they create an interface endpoint to it. 3) Model hosts run in their VPC with SGs restricting outbound to their NAT/egress only. 4) Configure route tables so 0.0.0.0/0 points to their NAT gateway. 5) Ensure no public IPs on model subnets.

jess_security: Need to confirm KMS/HSM access patterns and whether our side ever initiates new outbound sockets. If we host control-plane components in our account, VPCE service should be cross-account and enforce allowed principals. Also need to confirm DNS: Private DNS for the VPCE service will override public resolver — FinCorp must be ok with that.

katie_fincorp: Can confirm FinCorp security will not allow internet-bound traffic from subnets that host the inference instances. They'll permit NAT egress to their external firewall appliance only. Also they require traffic flow diagram and a list of ports/protocols.

alex_sales: Thanks — @eli_engineering and @jess_security can you list required ports and a minimal route table example I can share in the SOW? FinCorp wants this before next week's kickoff.

eli_engineering: Minimal egress ports: 443/tcp outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints (via VPCE) and optionally 80 if certificate challenges needed. For private artifact fetches (if we pull model layers via S3), we either use S3 gateway endpoints or they can mirror models into an internal registry. Suggest:

- No IGWs on model subnets
- Route table for model-subnet(s): 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxxx (customer NAT)
- Route table entries for VPCE interface: AWS-managed, no manual route required for interface endpoints inside the VPC but make sure SGs allow outbound 443 to the VPCE ENI IPs

Example AWS CLI snippet they can run to attach route table to subnet:
```
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-abc123 --subnet-id subnet-0fedcba
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-06ab12cd
```

Note: for cross-account VPC peering, you need route entries for the peer CIDR; for VPCE interface endpoints you do not.

jess_security: Additions from security: 1) Restrict SG egress on model hosts to the VPCE service SG and to the NAT gateway CIDR only. 2) Use endpoint policies on the VPCE service to restrict which principals (our customer account + our service principal) can connect. 3) Ensure Private DNS is enabled for the VPCE service so control-plane hostnames resolve to private IPs. 4) TLS mutual auth for control-plane is preferred; if not possible, use strict client cert pinning and mTLS for any management calls.

mike_solutions: What's the plan for model artifact retrieval? If we can't hit public S3, two options: S3 VPC Gateway endpoint + bucket policy locked to their VPC OR they mirror model tarballs into an internal object store accessible over the private network. Which is easier for them?

katie_fincorp: They prefer S3 gateway endpoint + bucket policy. Can you give the policy snippet?

eli_engineering: Example bucket policy to lock access to their VPC endpoint (replace IDs):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:*",
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-models/*","arn:aws:s3:::redwood-models"],
      "Condition": {
        "StringNotEquals": {"aws:sourceVpce": "vpce-0abc123def"}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

That blocks access unless through the VPC endpoint.

jess_security: Also add CloudTrail in their account to capture VPCE.accept/attach events, and keep VPC Flow Logs for the model subnets for 30 days during POC.

alex_sales: Perfect — last question from legal: data residency. FinCorp wants all inference request logs kept in their account. Can we route logs there?

eli_engineering: Yes — we can push audit logs (request metadata, not raw payloads unless contract allows) to a customer S3 bucket via cross-account role. Need bucket ARN + IAM role ARNs to allow PutObject. We'll provide a CloudFormation snippet for that.

katie_fincorp: I'll send the bucket ARN and their security contact. Also: they want a short diagram for architecture — can you attach before EOD?

alex_sales: Will do. @sre_bot can you generate a quick checklist and ping when the diagram is uploaded? :thumbsup:

sre_bot: Checklist created: "FinCorp POC - VPCE + NAT egress checklist". Items: request VPC CIDR, subnet IDs for model hosts, NAT gateway ID, VPCE ID, bucket ARN, security contacts, route table IDs. Added due date: 3 days.

mike_solutions: I'll start drafting the SOW snippet for the networking section and include the CLI snippets, SG examples, and the bucket policy. Will share a PR here when ready.

alex_sales: Thanks everyone — big help. I'll update FinCorp and share the diagram + SOW draft once Mike posts it.
